identity.title: OMAC: A Holistic Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration

problem.claim: The paper addresses holistic optimization of LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), where agents collaborate and communicate for complex tasks.

gap.claim: Existing development often relies on handcrafted methods, while systematic design and optimization of LLM-based MAS remains limited.

contributions.claim: Introduces OMAC, a general framework for holistic optimization of LLM-based MAS.

Defines five optimization dimensions spanning agent functionality and collaboration structure, and proposes a two-actor algorithm—the Semantic Initializer and Contrastive Comparator—to optimize any single dimension.
Presents an algorithm for joint optimization across multiple MAS dimensions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish OMAC as a general framework that holistically optimizes LLM-based MAS across five dimensions, including both agent functionality and collaboration structure.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show OMAC achieving superior performance on diverse tasks compared with recent approaches.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM agents and collaborative MAS are described as capable on complex applications and tasks.
MAS development is characterized as often handcrafted, with limited systematic design and optimization literature.
OMAC is introduced as a general framework for holistic MAS optimization.
The paper describes single-dimension optimization using two actors, followed by joint optimization across dimensions.
Extensive experiments are reported to show superior performance across diverse tasks against recent approaches.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports five optimization dimensions spanning agent functionality and collaboration structure, without enumerating them, then describes separate single-dimension and joint-optimization algorithms.

lessons.interpretation: Making optimization axes explicit can connect a broad systems objective to modular procedures and a later integrated procedure.
lessons.application: For a multi-component system paper, enumerate the main design axes before describing algorithms, and state whether each procedure optimizes one axis or several jointly.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the system has no meaningful separable dimensions or when joint interactions dominate and cannot be modularized.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five optimization dimensions, task identities, baselines, metrics, quantitative gains, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess the reported performance claim or the algorithms' implementation and limitations.

editorial_revisions.before: The abstract organizes the framework around five explicit optimization dimensions covering both agent functionality and collaboration structure, then provides separate single-dimension and joint-optimization algorithms.
editorial_revisions.after: The abstract reports five optimization dimensions spanning agent functionality and collaboration structure, without enumerating them, then describes separate single-dimension and joint-optimization algorithms.
